You are being evaluated on Continual-ARC, a lifelong stream of ARC-style grid puzzles.
Each puzzle instance has a task id and a test input grid. Tasks recur across the
stream with fresh inputs. Each instance is a separate conversation: the next one
starts without this one's messages.

On every message you must choose exactly one action and put it as a JSON object
on the last line of your reply:
  {"action": "submit", "grid": [[0, 1, 2], [3, 4, 5]]}   submit an output grid
  {"action": "request_demos"}                            ask for one more demonstration pair for this task
  {"action": "finish"}                                   end the instance, once it is over
Grids are lists of rows; cells are integers 0-9; dimensions are 1-30.

Each demo request returns one more input-output pair of the task, up to the demo cap shown
with the input.

Scoring: an instance you solve costs 1 for each wrong submission and 1 for
each demo request. An instance is over when a submission is correct or when the attempt
cap is reached, and one that ends unsolved costs the whole budget, 16, however
many submissions and demo requests it used. Feedback on a submission is only
correct/incorrect. There is no way to abandon an instance, and finish is refused until
the instance is over. Each instance is scored on its own, and lower cost is better.

In your continual harness, entries created without global_=True belong to this session and are lost with it.

import re
texts=[r['message']['content'][0]['text'] for r in recs if r.get('message',{}).get('role')=='user']
def extract_grid(section):
    return [[int(x) for x in line.split()] for line in section.strip().splitlines()]
pairs=[]
for txt in texts:
    for n in re.findall(r'Demo pair (\d+) input',txt):
        mi=re.search(rf'Demo pair {n} input \(\d+x\d+\):\n(.*?)\nDemo pair {n} output',txt,re.S)
        mo=re.search(rf'Demo pair {n} output \(\d+x\d+\):\n(.*?)(?:\n\nSame instance|\Z)',txt,re.S)
        pairs.append({'input':extract_grid(mi.group(1)),'output':extract_grid(mo.group(1))})
mt=re.search(r'Test input \(30x24\):\n(.*?)\nWrong attempts',texts[-1],re.S)
test=extract_grid(mt.group(1))
print(len(pairs),len(test),len(test[0]))

def transform(grid):
    g=[r[:] for r in grid]; H=len(g); W=len(g[0]); bg=g[0][0]
    # destination bands: rows with same non-bg border at both ends and one uniform interior
    dest={}; bandrows=set()
    r=0
    while r<H:
        row=g[r]
        if row[0]==row[-1] and row[0]!=bg and len(set(row[1:-1]))==1 and row[1]!=bg:
            start=r; border=row[0]; interior=row[1]
            while r<H and g[r]==row: r+=1
            end=r
            dest[interior]=(start,end,border)
            bandrows.update(range(start,end))
        else: r+=1
    # top objects = connected components outside bands, ignoring background
    seen=set(); objs=[]
    for r in range(H):
        if r in bandrows: continue
        for c in range(W):
            if g[r][c]==bg or (r,c) in seen: continue
            stack=[(r,c)]; seen.add((r,c)); cells=[]
            while stack:
                a,b=stack.pop(); cells.append((a,b))
                for da,db in ((1,0),(-1,0),(0,1),(0,-1)):
                    x,y=a+da,b+db
                    if 0<=x<H and 0<=y<W and x not in bandrows and g[x][y]!=bg and (x,y) not in seen:
                        seen.add((x,y)); stack.append((x,y))
            objs.append(cells)
    out=[r[:] for r in g]
    # erase source objects
    for cells in objs:
        for r,c in cells: out[r][c]=bg
        from collections import Counter
        outer=Counter(g[r][c] for r,c in cells).most_common(1)[0][0]
        inner=[(r,c) for r,c in cells if g[r][c]!=outer]
        def paste(paste_cells,color):
            if not paste_cells or color not in dest: return
            minr=min(r for r,c in paste_cells); maxr=max(r for r,c in paste_cells)
            start,end,b=dest[color]
            dr=end-1-maxr
            for r,c in paste_cells: out[r+dr][c]=b
        paste(cells,outer)
        paste(inner, g[inner[0][0]][inner[0][1]] if inner else None)
    return out
for i,p in enumerate(pairs):
    pred=transform(p['input']); print(i,pred==p['output'])
    if pred!=p['output']:
        print([(r,c,pred[r][c],p['output'][r][c]) for r in range(30) for c in range(24) if pred[r][c]!=p['output'][r][c]][:20])
